findings.finding: One member-value class still raises something other than Refused: an out-of-range JSON number in a digest-matched record. A member value of 1e400 or -1e400 parses to an infinite float, and canonical() then raises ValueError (out-of-range float) before the canonical-bytes comparison. An integer of more than 4300 digits makes parse() raise ValueError from Python's integer-string limit, which parse() does not catch. I probed both on c2 and c3 for imageDigest, target and treeRoot, and got ValueError on both. A 4300-digit integer is refused as stated ('root alias image differs'). This is the same class as RA-C1-2: shared helpers that the policy also uses, not introduced by this contract, and reached only with bytes pinned in the signed policy or supplied to prepare.py. Such bytes can never be canonical, so no admissible record is affected. It fails closed: launcher main() maps ValueError to FAIL with exit 2, and prepare.py, which has no handler for any refusal, ends in a traceback naming ValueError instead of a Refused reason.

Does the fix change the behaviour of any valid record? No. By construction: a treeRoot that is in the set of declared roots is already a str, so type(tree) is str removes only non-str values. The split target test computes the same predicate, with the same text, for every target that encodes. By probe: 13 valid records give byte-identical results on c2 and c3. These are the fixture, two aliases, an uppercase path, a 64-character name, an absolute target, a one-character target, a surrogate-escaped byte, a JSON surrogate pair, U+FFFF, an astral character, 4096-byte two-byte and escaped-byte targets, and another declared root. Only invalid records change: in the launcher, their FAIL reason changes from the TypeError or UnicodeEncodeError type name to Refused, with the same exit 2. Recommendation: adopt the fix as is.
